subject: Sovereign storage binding — options and verification steps
messages:
From: Markus Berg <markus.berg@greenfieldhealth.eu>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example
Cc: Greenfield Health Legal <legal@greenfieldhealth.eu>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sovereign storage: binding data to our EU-only storage — questions

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal and infra teams want clarity on how Redwood would guarantee that patient data stored via a Private/VPC deployment remains physically resident in our EU object store and can be deleted on our instruction. A few specific questions:

- Can Redwood be configured to write customer data only to a customer-provided S3 endpoint (we want to use our region-locked bucket)?
- What are the deletion guarantees and timelines for primary data vs backups/snapshots?
- How do you provide proof that data has been removed (attestation / logs)?
- What about caches and KV state on the inference runtime (are there in-memory or local disk artifacts that may persist)?

Attached is a short requirements memo from our legal team.

Can you outline options and a high-level verification playbook so we can review with our Security Ops?

Regards,
Markus
Director of Infrastructure
Greenfield Health

Markus — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi (Product Security) and Lauren (Private Deployments) so they can provide the technical and compliance details. High-level answer up front: yes, we support customer-provided object storage endpoints and HSM/KMS integration for key control; we can provide a signed deletion attestation and the operational playbook you can run with your Security Ops.

Next steps: Rishi will describe the verification steps and timelines. Lauren will outline the configuration options for S3-compatible endpoints, snapshot behavior, and runtime cache handling. I attached our vendor-facing overview (Sovereign-Storage-Options.pdf) which shows three deployment patterns.

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example
To: Markus Berg <markus.berg@greenfieldhealth.eu>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.example, neha_kapoor@redwood.example
Date: 2026-08-01T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sovereign storage: binding data to our EU-only storage — questions

Markus — quick technical run-through and recommended verification/playbook. I tried to avoid jargon where possible.

1) Storage binding options (recommended order):
   a) Customer-hosted S3 (recommended): Redwood writes all persistent objects (requests, logs, model artifacts you opt into) directly to your S3 endpoint in your account. We never provision storage in our cloud for that tenant. Access is via customer-provided credentials/assume-role.
   b) Customer-managed network file store behind VPC peering: Redwood runtime mounts a network share that lives in your VPC. Good for air-gapped environments.
   c) Redwood-managed storage with region lock: we host storage in the EU-only project and enforce routing policies and copy-reduction. (Less stringent than the first two.)

2) Key management and cryptographic control:
   - We support KMS/HSM bring-your-own-key (BYOK). Keys remain in your KMS; Redwood holds only a reference.
   - For BYOK, cryptographic erasure is the primary deletion mechanism for encrypted objects: destroy the KMS key and the ciphertext is unrecoverable. We document the key destroy event and provide a signed KMS audit snapshot.

3) Deletion timelines & guarantees (typical):
   - Primary object store: deletion issued by customer -> immediate delete request to S3 endpoint; confirmation within 24 hours.
   - Runtime caches / KV (ephemeral): flushed on process termination; we enforce a policy to zero memory for sensitive fields and rotate in-memory caches on deploy. Confirmation within 48 hours for full runtime cycle.
   - Backups/snapshots: depends on your snapshot lifecycle. If snapshots live in your S3 bucket we delete per your retention TTL; if we snapshot into a Redwood-managed vault (rare, with customer consent) deletion occurs within 30 days with an earlier secure-erase option available under contract.

4) Verification / Attestation options (we offer one or more depending on contract):
   - Signed deletion certificate: we produce a signed PDF that lists object keys, deletion timestamps, and KMS key destroy event IDs.
   - Audit logs: S3 server-side deletion events, KMS change logs, and runtime trace logs (obfuscated PII) zipped and delivered to a secure share.
   - Onsite or remote attestation run: our Ops team executes the deletion playbook while your Security Ops watches (or we provide video capture with logs).

5) Handling caches and model KV state:
   - KV caches are in-VM and encrypted at rest; we provide a purge API that removes KV entries and then restarts the serving processes.
   - We recommend ephemeral inference nodes with short-lived lifecycles for sensitive tenants; that drastically reduces persistent local state.

6) Recommended verification playbook (short):
   Step 0: Agree scope (object keys, snapshot ids, cache types).
   Step 1: Customer issues deletion request via the Console/Support ticket containing target keys and a confirmation signature.
   Step 2: Redwood runs delete operation against your S3 + calls KMS Destroy (if BYOK requested).
   Step 3: Redwood rotates serving nodes, purges caches, and clears KV.
   Step 4: We aggregate deletion evidence: S3 DeleteMarker records, KMS event id, node restart logs, snapshot lifecycle events.
   Step 5: We deliver signed deletion certificate + audit bundle within SLA windows.

SLA examples (negotiable): primary delete confirmation 24–72 hours; full audit bundle within 7 days.

I'll attach the playbook draft and an egress diagram (see attachments from Stephanie). Lauren, can you add implementation notes for S3 assume-role and network firewall rules?

Regards,
Rishi
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.example
To: Markus Berg <markus.berg@greenfieldhealth.eu>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.example

Subject: Re: Sovereign storage: binding data to our EU-only storage — questions

Markus — implementation notes and firewall/network checklist below. I'm also including practical notes we recommend customers confirm before go-live.

S3/endpoint configuration notes:
- We support S3-compatible endpoints (AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph RGW). We recommend using an IAM role with least privilege: PutObject, GetObject, DeleteObject, ListObject (limited to tenant prefix).
- Use a dedicated bucket with tenant prefix and block public access at the bucket level.
- Configure bucket lifecycle to avoid unintended snapshot retention. If you want immutable WORM, coordinate exceptions with us — WORM buckets will prevent deletion until lifecycle expires.

Network & routing checklist:
- VPC peering/PrivateLink: ensure port range TCP 443 allowed between Redwood runtime subnets and your S3 endpoints.
- DNS: provide a private DNS entry if your S3 sits on private network.
- Egress logging: enable access logs for the bucket and share a read-only log sink so Redwood can push deletion events.

Backup & snapshot handling:
- If you opt for our managed snapshot service (contract add-on), we store encrypted snapshots in an EU-only project. For maximum assurance, use our BYOK flow so key destroy can cryptographically render snapshots unrecoverable.
- For customer-hosted snapshots, your retention config rules apply; we will not create additional backups outside your storage.

Operational cautions and recommended language for contract: 
- Include explicit language that customer-supplied storage endpoints are the authoritative store for customer data.
- Define deletion windows and what constitutes "evidence" (S3 DeleteMarker, KMS event id, node logs).
- Specify any permitted exceptions (legal hold, regulatory retention) and the escalation path.

Attachments: 
- Sovereign-Storage-Options.pdf: diagrams and the three patterns Rishi mentioned.
- egress_flowchart.png: shows network flow and where deletion/Audit hooks occur.
- deletion-playbook-draft.docx: the step-by-step checklist we will run with your Security Ops.

If this looks good, we can schedule a 45-minute run-through with your Security Ops to walk the playbook and perform a dry-run. Available slots: Aug 6 or Aug 10.

Cheers,
Lauren
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments

Subject: Re: Sovereign storage: binding data to our EU-only storage — questions

Thanks — this is very helpful and thorough. A few follow-ups from Legal and Security Ops after reviewing the playbook: 

- Legal wants the signed deletion certificate to include the KMS key fingerprint and the KMS key destroy transaction id (we will record both in our ledger).
- Security Ops asks for a one-time cryptographic hash of the tenant prefix before deletion so we can verify post-delete (we understand it will be one-way, just a pre-delete HMAC with a shared secret).
- We want the dry-run on Aug 10 at 09:00 UTC and will bring two members from our Security Ops and one from Legal.

Can you confirm the dry-run will produce the exact audit bundle (S3 delete markers, KMS audit event, node logs) and that Redwood will provide the signed certificate including KMS destroy id? Also, please confirm Redwood's retention of platform metadata logs that are not customer-controlled (e.g., request routing metrics) — we assume those remain under Redwood's control for 90 days unless contractually extended.

If you can confirm those points, we'll lock the Aug 10 slot.

Regards,
Markus
